ledger.event: F42 and F43 issued together at base cafac16, the sitting's second pair of siblings, proved disjoint at the files before either envelope was written. F42 takes S19, the last open spark that had a lane, and it is a correction of a half-proved fix rather than new ground: F35 landed splitCheck as case-sensitive AND last-wins with a fixture for the first half only, so restoring first-match while keeping case-sensitivity leaves the self-test green. The envelope therefore dictates a mutation PER ITEM that reds for that item alone, and says so in those words, because a single mutation that reds two items leaves one untested. It also takes the two gaps F35 named and did not take: a quoted YAML scalar carrying its quote characters into the id, the kind and the title, which YAML permits a child to write anywhere, and a child's kind of reject being mapped to portable so an explicit do-not-absorb signal is inverted into a candidate intake. F43 exists because this sitting paid for it twice. Both seats were launched from the qwen-code recipe exactly as written, and both read their packet, analysed correctly and wrote nothing, because that harness defaults to requiring approval for every edit and shell command and a print-mode seat has no terminal to approve at. The recipe has never named a mode, so no seat launched from that line could ever write. F43 names the mode on the one harness whose help output the control plane actually ran, and DICTATES that the three uninstalled harnesses declare the gap instead of guessing, because a guessed flag fails silently in exactly the way the qwen line just did and T07 is the trap for a recipe remembered rather than read. Two things about the issuance itself belong in the record. The tool policy refused to write F43's envelope through a shell heredoc, reading the flag named in the prose as an attempt to create an unsafe agent; the envelope was written with a file tool instead and its text now describes the option rather than spelling it, which is a constraint on how this control plane can document a launch line, not a safety judgement about the lane. And the seat packet went over its 26 KB cap again on the Now line and was compacted three times to 1471 characters to fit, which is the fourth time this sitting that the board's own prose has been the binding constraint on a writer's context.

F42 and F43 both returned CORRECTIONS NEEDED on the same shape, and the control plane's own envelopes are the cause, which is D-62. D-61 had already narrowed the rule to: an acceptance item names its mutation at the production entry point. Both envelopes obeyed it and both still let an untested property ship, because the rule counts mutations per ITEM and an item can carry several properties. F42's item 3 carried three: a reject row is held, the match is case-insensitive, and the refusal is read before the floors. One mutation was named, the first was proved, and the control plane drove the other two itself after the review named them: dropping the toLowerCase in portableOf, and swapping the refusal check to sit after the check floor, each leaves alumni --self-test printing ok at exit 0, because the only reject fixture is already lowercase and already clears every floor. That is precisely the defect F42 existed to correct in F35, reproduced one level up by the envelope that ordered the correction. F43's item 3 carried a scope claim, every recipe the list command prints, and the implementation read scope as every recipe rendering a stdin carrier; the envelope's own words, its carrier line, invited that. goose renders no carrier, a property that predates the lane, so goose is invisible to the check while being one of the three recipes item 2 names, and deleting goose's unverified note leaves seat --self-test green while the same deletion on aider or opencode correctly reds.

F43 landed from writer/F43 at 75f5d1d, fast-forward, after one correction, and it closes every lane booked this sitting. A print-mode launch line now names the harness's approval mode, absorbed as T80, and the lane exists because this sitting paid for it twice: two seats were launched from a recipe that had never named one, and both read their packet, did correct work in their heads and wrote nothing, because the harness default requires approval for every edit and shell command and a print-mode seat has no terminal to give it. F44 and F45 issued together at base ab398c3, proved disjoint, and they take two of the four sparks that ended this sitting's booked work with no lane. F44 takes S22: the census counts processes rather than seats, six rows for two launches, and F40 landing did NOT fix it because every one of those rows carries the harness token in program position, so T77 names it as a limit and this lane closes it by folding a launch's process tree through the parent pid the lister already can report. F45 takes S23, the one that cost a paid session here: a correction envelope is written to main while a seat reads its envelope from its own worktree, which still sits at the issuance commit holding the superseded page, and git fetch does not touch the working tree. The seat path will refuse and write NOTHING to stdout, because the launch line is a pipe into the harness and an empty stdin is a loud failure, while a comparison that cannot be made is a NOTE and not a refusal, since a check that cannot pass is T09 and this factory has shipped one before. F45 is the delicate one and the envelope says so: the gate runs packet.mjs from an unpacked archive with no git, CI checks out shallow, and F31's byte-stable prefix is a 95 to 97 per cent cache hit this sitting, so nothing the lane adds may reach stdout in any path. Issuing the pair put the seat packet over its 26 KB cap again and the shed was found where D-58 says to look before firing its trigger. The traps digest had grown from 11.4 KB to 12.3 as this sitting wrote five trap rows, and a rule that names a check compresses to its FIRST SENTENCE, so four rules from the previous sitting, T72 T73 T74 and T75, were carrying 200 to 256 characters of evidence into every seat's digest because each was written as one sentence with no internal period. Splitting the rule from its evidence in each took the packet from 100.1 per cent to 97.8 while traps.yaml GREW to 22925 bytes. That is the second time this sitting the same mechanism has paid: detail written for a person reading the file costs a seat nothing, and per-lane scoping stays deferred with its trigger unfired.

F44 returned at 2d79199 and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED, having approved the fold and then found two failures neither the envelope nor the control plane had named, both driven again by the control plane at the objects. The walk assumes the process listing is a complete, acyclic, single-instant snapshot in which every ancestor pid resolves to a row, and on this machine that is false twice: Windows stamps ParentProcessId at creation and never clears it when the parent dies, and Get-CimInstance does not enumerate atomically. First, two counted rows whose parent pids point at each other, which ordinary pid-reuse churn produces, each fold into the other and BOTH vanish: the census prints 0 running writer seats for two live harness processes. That is worse than the over-count this lane exists to fix, because the two-writer ceiling and the dead-seat resume read this number, so a false zero lets a third seat launch and lets a resume collide with a session still running. Second, a counted row whose parent is absent from the listing, having exited between the enumeration and the write, cannot be attached to its launch and is counted as a second seat, which is precisely the S22 shape the lane was issued to close, reopened by churn rather than by any path the two required mutations touch.

F45 returned at 7a828e5 and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED on a defect worse than the one the lane closes. The two new fixtures cover no repository at all, and a repository whose copies DIFFER. Neither covers the case every ordinary launch takes, where the comparison succeeds and the copies are IDENTICAL, so that branch has no fixture that could fail it. Driven by the control plane at the objects: replacing if (same) return null with if (false) return null leaves packet --self-test printing ok at exit 0, while packet seat F45 on a clean byte-identical worktree exits 3 with ZERO bytes on stdout and refuses. Every lane, every worktree, with no correction pending, would refuse and no seat could launch, and the self-test, the check and the landing gate would all stay green. That is exactly what T09 and the envelope's own item 2 forbid, and the envelope is the cause: it named three mutations, drop the refusal, make the unresolvable case refuse, and leak the note to stdout, and never named the equality comparison itself as a property. D-62 for the third and fourth time in one sitting, now in both siblings at once. The review also found the log claiming sizeBudget printed 70 budgets where it prints 71, every KB and percent figure beside it being correct, which is the fourth uncommanded count this sitting. What the review cleared, having driven it: the refusal writes nothing to stdout and exits 3 naming the difference and the remedy, an unresolvable comparison notes and emits proved from an unpacked archive with no git, stdout is byte-identical between the two paths at 32226 bytes, and the gate is 21 of 21.

Sitting 11 closed at the owner's word after six lanes landed: F40, F41, F42, F43, F44 and F45. The tenure is D-63 and nothing of it is left in the session - what landed, what the reviews cost and bought, the four things this control plane got wrong, how a seat is actually launched on this machine, and the state a successor inherits. The finding of the sitting is D-62, and it is sitting 10's finding one level deeper. D-61 had narrowed the rule to: an acceptance item names its mutation at the production entry point. Every envelope this sitting obeyed that and four still shipped an untested property, because the rule counts mutations per ITEM while an item carries several properties. Six independent reviews found six blocking defects the control plane's own verification had missed, six for six, and every one traced back to an envelope that named the mutations it could imagine and left the ordinary case unnamed. The worst was F45, where the fixtures covered no-repository and copies-differ but never copies-identical, so forcing the comparison to report a difference left the self-test, the check AND the landing gate green while every launch in the factory would have refused with empty stdout. What replaces the old reading: a mutation per PROPERTY, a universal claim proved at the member most likely to ESCAPE it, and a fixture proves a property only if the fixture COULD FAIL IT. The tier did not change and the evidence now supports that: deepseek-flash produced six landed lanes, took correction accurately every time it was told exactly what to do, twice closed holes the envelope had not named, and once caught its own assertion failing to be falsifiable and re-anchored it unprompted. F46 to F49 are booked for the four open sparks, proved disjoint by six pairwise commands rather than one call that would have answered about a single pair. Three of those four are a rule that is now wrong or incomplete - T70, T76 and T81's own remedy - which is what a factory looks like when its checks are new enough to still be learning their own boundaries. Nothing is running, no envelope is issued, no experiment is open, the gate is 21 of 21, and the Sonnet reviewer permission expired with the sitting.

F47 and F48 issued together at base d4427d7, sitting 12's first pair of siblings, proved disjoint by six PAIRWISE runs of seat.mjs disjoint over the whole queue rather than one call that would have answered about a single pair. They take the two sparks that sit on the landing path of every other lane this sitting. F47 takes S24: gate steps run as spawnSync bash -e with a Windows script path and a Windows cwd, and when bash resolves to the WSL launcher every one of the 21 reds at any commit, including a commit green from git-bash a second later. Two seats paid for that last sitting and the gate prints step NAMES with stderr going to a log file, so the cause is invisible from inside a print-mode seat. The envelope's load-bearing instruction is the probe's FORM: it must be a script file in logDir run as bash -e with cwd workDir, because a probe shaped like bash -c true succeeds under the WSL launcher and would leave all 21 reds where they are, which is T09 shipped as a fix. That is named as its own acceptance property with its own mutation. F48 takes S25: pathCitations reads any backticked token with a slash and a source extension as a tree path, so the revision spec that F45's log cited was rejected although git rev-parse prints its blob, costing a control-plane documentation fix because that lane's correction was spent. The envelope forbids resolving the rev with git and says why at the object: rule H runs inside the gate from an unpacked archive that is not a repository, files() already falls back to a directory walk there, so a git rev-parse would pass on this disk and be unable to run where the gate runs. The path part carries the whole of the evidence, since an invented rev spec still names a file that is not in the tree. F48 also grew by one class found at the objects while its envelope was written, not booked from a spark: running the shipping regex over a backticked https URL ending .md shows it comes back as a citation and would be rejected, while CONTROL_PLANE.md section 2 instructs the control plane to record exactly such a URL. It is the same defect - the extractor never asks what KIND of token it has - so it joined the lane and the board title was widened rather than a second lane being booked. Both envelopes carry SIX acceptance properties each, one mutation apiece that must red for that property ALONE, which is D-62 applied at issue for the first time. In both the ordinary case is named explicitly as a property with a fixture that could fail it, because that is precisely what F45's fixtures lacked. Issuance cost the same fight the last sitting recorded four times: both envelopes came in over the 6 KB one-page cap, at 7289 and 7005 bytes, and were cut to 6088 and 6115 by deleting narrative rather than properties - the F45 lesson compressed to one sentence in each, and in F47 two lines the Holds line and the Acceptance block already carried.

F47 landed from writer/F47 at de42916, fast-forward, after one correction, and S24 is absorbed by REWRITING T70 rather than adding a row - the move F44 got when it closed the limit T77 named. T70 had said gate steps run through bash from a file and are unaffected by shell dialect; that sentence was false on this machine and two seats last sitting spent calls proving a 21-step red was not their own. The gate now probes its shell in a step's OWN form before the first step and exits 2 with one diagnostic naming the shell, the probe, the cwd and the shell's own stderr. The rewritten T70 carries a Check is sentence, so the digest compresses it to its first sentence and the seat packet fell from 99.8 to 99.6 per cent of cap while traps.yaml grew - the third time that mechanism has paid. The correction is the part to read, and both the independent review and the control plane found it separately by driving the same mutation: every fixture exercised the library functions and NOTHING exercised the lines wiring them into the command a person types. Replacing the CLI's shellStop call with a null left landingGate --self-test ok at exit 0, kitCheck ok and GATE PASSED while the lane did nothing, which is D-61 in its own words and F45's shape reproduced by the very envelope that named F45 as the thing to look hardest at. The seat's answer was better than the correction asked for: it made the shell selectable by GATE_SHELL, added a fixture that spawns the SHIPPED FILE as a process and asserts the probe ran before the archive was unpacked, added correction B's spawn-cause fixture, and then added a NINTH property nobody dictated - that with GATE_SHELL unset the gate still spawns bash - because the envelope had only flagged default drift under Look hardest at. That is the second sitting running in which a sweep seat closed a hole the envelope did not name. It also disclosed, rather than hid, that fixture 7 needs a repository to resolve a commit and is therefore SKIPPED where the gate runs the self-test from an unpacked archive. The control plane verified that at the objects: with no .git present the wiring can be removed and the self-test still prints ok at exit 0. So the property is proved by a command a person runs from a checkout and NOT by the gate that protects main. The seat's correction cap was spent and AGENTS section 3 says split rather than take a third round, so the remainder is booked as F50 with the seat's own named remedy - fixture 7 builds its own throwaway repository.
